scene.note: Links turn two separate files into a small site, and let a visitor reach a section, an email or a call in one click.

steps.note: A visitor wants class times. The home page says they are on the classes page, but nothing leads there.
Wrap the words that name the classes page in a link, with the other file's name as its address.
One click takes the visitor from the home page to Kofi's classes page.
On the classes page, the line about going back is plain text, so the visitor is stuck.
Make that line a link to the home page, in the same folder.
The visitor can move between the two pages in both directions.
The home page has three sections, and the Jump to line names them.
Give each section heading a name with an id, so a link can point at it.
Each word on the Jump to line links to its id, and the page scrolls straight there.
Under Visit us, the email address and the phone number are plain text.
Wrap each one in a link whose address starts with the scheme for email or for calls.
A tap on a phone starts an email or a call to the studio, with nothing to copy by hand.
